chunks.text: Today we will talk about Peru.
Peru is a beautiful and diverse country in South America.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Peru?
Peru is in South America.
It is next to Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil, Bolivia, and Chile.
To the west, Peru touches the Pacific Ocean.
It has mountains, rainforests, deserts, and beaches.
What is the capital city of Peru?
The capital city is Lima.
Lima is on the Pacific Coast.
It is the largest city in Peru.
Lima has museums, markets, historic buildings, and modern neighborhoods.
It is a mix of old and new.
Other cities in Peru include Cusco, Arequipa, Trujillo, and Iquitos.
How many people live in Peru?
About 34 million people live in Peru.
Many people live in cities near the coast or in the mountains.
Some people live in small towns and remote villages in the Andes or Amazon jungle.
Peru has many ethnic groups and indigenous cultures.
What language do people speak in Peru?
The official language is Spanish.
Many people also speak Quechua or Aymara, which are indigenous languages.
In some areas, people speak Amazonian languages.
English is spoken in some schools, tourist areas, and businesses.
What is the weather like in Peru?
Peru has different climates in different regions.
On the coast, it is dry and warm.
In the mountains, it is cooler with a rainy season and a dry season.
In the Amazon rainforest, it is hot and humid all year.
Peru has many kinds of weather because of its geography.
What does Peru look like?
Peru has many landscapes.
The Andes Mountains, the Amazon rainforest, the coastline with beaches and cities, the desert especially near Lima, the sacred valley and Lake Titicaca.
Peru is a country with rich nature and historic sites.
What animals live in Peru?
In Peru, you can see llamas and alpacas in the mountains, monkeys, jaguars, and sloths in the jungle, condors, very large birds, frogs, snakes, and many insects.
In the ocean, you can see sea lions, penguins, and whales.
Peru is one of the world's most biodiverse countries.
What do people eat in Peru?
Peruvian food is famous and full of flavor.
People eat rice, potatoes, and corn, chicken, fish, and beef, vegetables, chili peppers, and herbs.

Popular dishes, ceviche, raw fish with lime, onion, and chili, lomo saltado, beef stir -fried with onions and tomatoes, ajide gallina, chicken in a creamy spicy sauce, papa a la huancaina, potatoes with cheese sauce.
Peru has over 3,000 types of potatoes.
What do people drink in Peru?

People drink chicha morada, a sweet drink made from purple corn, Inca cola, a yellow soda popular in Peru, mate de coca, coca leaf tea, especially in the mountains, fruit juices from mango, papaya, or passion fruit, coffee and herbal teas.
What is life like in Peru?
Life in Peru is different in each region.
In the cities, people go to school, work, and shops.
In the mountains and jungle, life is more traditional and connected to nature.
Many people work in farming, fishing, tourism, handicrafts like weaving and pottery.
People value family, festivals, and community.
What are some holidays and traditions in Peru?
Inti Ramey, Festival of the Sun in June in Cusco, Carnival with Dancing in Water Fights, Samana Santa, Holy Week before Easter, Independence Day, July 28th, All Saints Day, November 1st.
People wear traditional clothes, especially in the highlands.
Music and dance are part of every celebration.
Instruments like pan flutes and drums are popular.
Some fun facts about Peru.
Peru is home to Machu Picchu, an ancient Inca city.
The Nazca lines are giant drawings on the desert floor.
The Inca Empire was once the largest in the Americas.
Peru is the birthplace of potatoes, quinoa, and alpacas.
The flag is red and white.
Now you know many things about Peru.
You know where it is, what people speak, and what they eat.
You learned about the nature, food, animals, and traditions.
Great job.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
